pairs.why: A keeps a slightly softer pink ground and richer greens with some darker shade variation, while B pushes the ground to hotter magenta and the map to a yellower lime.
A's backpack body is a deeper mid-green with lime kept for trim, matching the real card, while B lets bright lime take over the flap and pockets.
The real hero objects are saturated and colorful, and B's orange rover on warm ground has that chroma, while A's white and gray rover on gray ground is nearly neutral.
The real card has a loud saturated red cooler, deep blue and warm gold sand, which A matches, while B is washed out and dusty; A does add extra hue families (starfish, ball, palm).
Both use the same cobalt-and-gold drums on a hot pink-magenta rayed ground that is brighter than the real dark purple, so color gives no reason to choose.
A's lavender-pink stone and navy squares are slightly closer to the real violet-gray stone, and both have similar saturated grass.
Both put a gold rope with a red accent on a purple wavy ground, so the palette gives no clear separation.
B's teal ground, dark navy lamp and neutral truss with only the yellow, cyan and red lights are closer to the real card than A's extra orange band and deeper blue ground.
